issue: org.kde.desktop/Breeze gives an app-owned QQC2.ToolTip a Tooltip role at its root while its shared background can resolve as Window. R80's original root-pixel capture also showed two test hints at the same coordinates; its background-object colorSet observation remains valid, but that pixel comparison was ambiguous.

change.application: plasma/applets/org.irixclassic.applications/contents/ui/ConfigGeneral.qml replaces its shared attached tooltip with an app-owned QQC2.ToolTip and explicitly binds its content/background to Kirigami.Theme.Tooltip
change.gallery: plasma/tests/galerias-nativas/plasma_style_demo.py gives its two local scrollbar tips explicit Tooltip-role content/background

gallery_matrix.runtime: Qt 6.8.2, org.kde.desktop, private XDG palette profile, actual project plasma_style_demo QML, Xephyr :84

application_component_probe.source_component: The QQC2.ToolTip block extracted from ConfigGeneral.qml; translation call substituted with a sample string in the isolated wrapper

limits: The applet KCM was not launched as a full Plasma configuration module; its exact Tooltip QML block was exercised inside an isolated Qt Quick wrapper, with only the translated text expression substituted.
The gallery tests one vertical scrollbar hint per run; the horizontal tooltip uses the same QML role composition but was not separately hovered in R88.

The workaround applies to Qt Quick tooltips owned by this project. Other applications using the upstream shared attached tooltip may still use Window for the background; changing KDE source or providing a Qt Quick Controls style is outside this item.
This is toolkit/palette behavior evidence, not a historical DomainOS pixel match or human approval.
conclusion: Project-owned Qt Quick tooltips now use the current KDE Tooltip background and text roles without modifying installed KDE sources. Rendered pixels followed DomainOS, Irixium, BreezeLight, BreezeDark and a contrasting yellow fixture; the ConfigGeneral component retained a delayed tooltip above its button and closed on leave.
